stage: the PC-chat dangling-target message now states the runtime's real consequence
what_changed: the check itself already existed and was already probed: a node whose nextNodeId or choice target does not exist is reported. What was missing was the CONSEQUENCE. I read the runtime lookup - OldPcUi.Chat.PendingChoiceNode uses chat.Nodes.TryGetValue and treats a miss as 'nothing pending' - so the thread does not error and does not advance: it simply stops, and the player is left without a next line. The message now says that, names TryGetValue, and both facts are asserted in the probe
why_it_matters: the message is what Studio shows an author. 'The branch will break' is vague; 'the runtime treats the miss as no continuation, so the thread stops silently' tells the author what they will see in the game and why nothing crashes
no_behaviour_change: the validation logic is untouched: only the text and the assertions around it changed
own_mistake: this receipt was MISSING from the commit that shipped the change, because the script that writes it had a syntax error (a bracket instead of an assignment) and the commit went out with only check.log and the probe. It is added here, separately, rather than by rewriting the pushed commit
